title: Europe Says 'No Way!' to Selling the World Cup to Private Investors
summary: Have you ever loved something so much you'd refuse to play if someone tried to sell it? That's exactly what's happening in soccer right now. European soccer leaders are so angry they voted to boycott the World Cup — the biggest soccer tournament on Earth — if Fifa, the sport's boss, goes ahead with a plan to sell parts of it to private investors. On Thursday, all 55 European soccer associations met in an emergency online meeting. The mood was described as 'venomous' — that means really, really angry. They say the World Cup isn't just a product you can buy and sell. 'The World Cup is not for sale,' Uefa, Europe's soccer group, said firmly. So what's the big fuss? Fifa president Gianni Infantino wants to create a new company, called Fifa Forward Enterprise, to run big events like the men's and women's World Cups. Then, outside investors could buy small shares in it. Infantino even wrote to Fifa's 211 members promising them $40 million each if they vote yes. He set a deadline of September 19 for them to accept. One of the investors could be Thrive Eternal, a firm founded by Joshua Kushner — whose brother Jared is married to former U.S. President Donald Trump's daughter. But Europe isn't budging. If the plan passes, they'll skip all Fifa tournaments, including the Women's World Cup play-offs in October. 'The World Cup cannot be treated as an investment product,' Uefa said. 'It is one of football's greatest sporting legacies.' For now, the ball is in Fifa's court.
why_it_matters: If you love a sport, this shows that sometimes the people who run it might try to make money from it, and it's okay for fans and teams to stand up when they think the game is being treated like a product.

keywords.explanation: A boycott is when people refuse to take part in something to show they disagree with it.
Venomous means full of anger or poison, like a snake's bite.
Uefa is the group that runs soccer in Europe.
Fifa is the world organization that makes the rules for soccer and runs the World Cup.
Private investors are people or companies who put money into something so they can earn more money later.
Gianni Infantino is the president of Fifa, the big boss of world soccer.

background_read: FIFA organizes the World Cup every four years, and it is watched by billions of people around the world.
Sometimes sports organizations look for ways to raise money, like selling shares to private investors, but fans worry this might change how the game is run.
In the past, boycotts have been used by countries and athletes to protest decisions they thought were unfair.
Article_Structure: WHO: All 55 European soccer associations, led by Uefa.
WHAT: They voted to boycott all Fifa tournaments if Fifa sells part of the World Cup to private investors.
WHERE: During an emergency online meeting.
WHY: Because they believe the World Cup is a sporting legacy, not something you can buy and sell like a product.

perspectives.description: Some people think that selling shares could bring in a lot of money to help make the World Cup even better and support soccer in poorer countries.
Many in Europe believe the World Cup is a proud tradition and should not be sold, because outside investors might make decisions for profit instead of what is best for the game.
Fans might be torn between wanting more money for the sport and worrying that the World Cup could change in ways they don't like if it is run by private companies.
